newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas shares end firmer in slow, cautious trade.
newsitem.headline: Caracas shares end firmer in slow, cautious trade.

text.p: Share prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange edged up in slow trade as investors took cautious positions while awaiting more positive news on privatizations and other policies, brokers said.
The market's 19-share index rose 0.57 percent to 4,614.54, as 17 stocks rose, nine fell and 10 closed flat.
"The rise in prices was slim, as was the volume. Investors seemed very cautious, which meant that trading was slow," one broker said.
Trading volume was again light with just 1.429 billion bolivars worth ($3 million) changing hands, the exchange said.

News that the government planned to place 10 percent of Banco de Venezuela and Banco Consolidado on the local market in forthcoming privatizations had encouraged market optimism, brokers said. But recent privatization setbacks meant that investors would wait to see the sales finalized before acting on the news.

Among leading stocks, benchmark Electricidad de Caracas rose 1.00 bolivar to 391.00 bolivars, steel company Sivensa rose 2.10 bolivars to 286.10 bolivars and agri-industrial company Mavesa edged up 0.50 bolivar to 126.50 bolivars.
